messages:
kai: ran a replay with the new queueing-emulator (policy=aggressive_prefetch) against week-of-prod trace, ~1.9M requests. quick summary: tokens/sec +11%, cost/unit -5%, but p99 latency for short sequences (<=64) jumped ~8%.

maria: ugh, short seqs are our tail-sensitive flows. do you have the kv-warmup hit rate and kernel-choice breakdown?

kai: yep. kv warmup for those traces dropped from 94% -> 71% for short seqs under the new prefetch timing. kernel selection shifted to fused_attn_v2 for ~83% of steps (was ~60%). profiling snippet below:

```
kernel_choice: fused_attn_v2: 83%
kernel_choice: native_dot: 12%
kv_cache_hit: short_seq: 71% -> 94% (baseline)
cpu_util: +6% overall
batch_size_mean: 11 -> 16
p99_short_seq: 22ms -> 24ms (+8%)
```

sam: interesting — fused_attn_v2 improves throughput but slightly regresses latency on tiny batches due to kernel startup overheads. also prefetch changed KV eviction horizon?

olivia: can you paste the queueing-emulator config you used? want to reproduce locally in the replay harness.

kai: sure. command and config I ran in the offline harness:

```
./replay_emulator --trace week_prod.pb --policy aggressive_prefetch \ 
  --token_budget_target 3072 --kv_prefetch_ms 12 --batch_window_ms 8 \ 
  --kernel_policy auto_select
```

and the policy JSON (excerpt):

```
{
  "name": "aggressive_prefetch",
  "kv_prefetch_ms": 12,
  "token_budget_target": 3072,
  "batch_window_ms": 8,
  "prefer_small_kernel_for_short_seq": false
}
```

maria: thanks. maybe the token_budget_target is too high for feeds with many short sequences — we bulk more tokens into a window and force fused kernels that favor throughput at tail cost. try per-model token_budget_target or adaptive target by recent seq-length histogram.

sam: agree. quick AB idea: run two replays over same trace: A) token_budget_target=3072 + prefer_small_kernel_for_short_seq=false, B) token_budget_target=1536 + prefer_small_kernel_for_short_seq=true. track p50/p95/p99 by seq-length buckets and cost/unit. set alert if p99_short_seq increases >3% or cost/unit increases >4%.

kai: i kicked off that AB locally. initial pass results (short run):

A: p99_short_seq 24ms, cost/unit 0.95
B: p99_short_seq 21ms, cost/unit 1.01

so B improves p99 but cost per token slightly higher. need longer run and shadow test.

olivia: reminds me we should check kernel scheduling fairness. fused_attn_v2 can starve tiny batches on some GPUs if kernels get queued. add kernel_scheduling_bias metric to the harness (time_in_kernel_queue by kernel).

perf-bot: automated profile summary generated: fused_attn_v2 queue_latency 3.6ms median, native_dot queue_latency 1.2ms median. kernel_swap_count: 42k. recommended: consider dynamic budget that lowers token_budget_target when short_seq_ratio > 0.6. :gear:

maria: decision proposal: 1) run 48h AB on full week trace with A/B configs above, 2) instrument kernel_queue_latency and kv_warmup by seq bucket, 3) if B yields p99_short_seq <= baseline and cost/unit within +3% accept for canary. rollback if p99_short_seq > +3% or customer-facing error rate increases.

sam: +1. i'll add the kernel_queue_latency metric to the replay harness and a dashboard. also adding a small simulation that approximates kernel startup cost vs batch size to predict crossover points for different GPUs.

kai: timeline: start AB tomorrow 00:00 UTC, run 48h. i'll upload raw replay artifacts to s3://redwood-replay/experiments/1798123456. tagging @eng-runtime for visibility.

olivia: can we also feed the A/B config into the A/B eval harness that runs eval prompts (prompt set: promptset_perf_tiny) so we check quality regressions?

maria: yes please. quality must be in the stop criteria. add eval harness threshold: log-likelihood delta per-token <= 0.005 and ngram BLEU diff <= 0.01.

kai: noted. will run eval harness nightly during the 48h AB. rough checklist posted in thread.

perf-bot: AB job scheduled: job_id=rb-1798123456-ab. start=1798209600 end=1798382400. notifications on #eng-runtime and #incidents if stop criteria hit.

maria: thanks team. follow-ups: once AB completes, we should test a hybrid approach: adaptive token_budget_target that decays for queues dominated by <=64 tokens. that might give both p99 and cost wins.

sam: agreed. capturing action items in a GH issue.

kai: closing loop — will post final artifacts and short writeup after AB completes. :rocket:
